newsitem.title: ITALY: Cuba's Castro ends visit to Italy, flies home.
newsitem.headline: Cuba's Castro ends visit to Italy, flies home.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro left Italy on Wednesday at the end of a high-profile visit crowned by an historic Vatican audience with Pope John Paul.
Officials at Rome's Fiumicino airport said a plane with Castro and his entourage had taken off bound for Havana.
Castro, one of the world's few remaining communist leaders, invited the Polish-born Pope at their audience on Tuesday to visit Cuba next year.
Both sides said the invitation had no conditions attached and had been accepted by the Pope, who was a major influence on the collapse of communism in eastern Europe.

Castro arrived in Italy last Saturday for a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit, where he blasted the 34-year-old U.S. embargo on Cuba and launched a sharp attack on what he called the evils of capitalism.

His stay in Rome, surrounded by some of the heaviest security seen in the Italian capital, also included talks with Italian political and business leaders and a final sightseeing visit to the ancient Forum earlier on Wednesday.
